body.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> is the cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) of the modifications (<s>vṛtti</s>) of the mind (<s>citta</s>). ||1.2||
Then the Seer abides in its own true nature. ||1.3||
Otherwise, [there is] identification with the modifications (<s>vṛtti</s>). ||1.4||
The modifications are fivefold, [either] afflicted (<s>kliṣṭa</s>) or non-afflicted (<s>akliṣṭa</s>). ||1.5||
[They are:] valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>), sleep (<s>nidrā</s>), and memory (<s>smṛti</s>). ||1.6||
Direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>āgama</s>) are the [means of] valid cognition. ||1.7||
Error (<s>viparyaya</s>) is false knowledge not based on the true form [of its object]. ||1.8||
Conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) is [a modification] following verbal knowledge, devoid of [a corresponding] object. ||1.9||
Sleep (<s>nidrā</s>) is the modification based on the cognition of absence. ||1.10||
Memory (<s>smṛti</s>) is the non-loss of experienced objects. ||1.11||
The cessation of these [modifications] is [achieved] through practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). ||1.12||

body.text: tatra sthitau yatno '-bhyāsaḥ ||1.13|| sa [?] tu [?] [ ] dīrgha-kāla-nairantarya-satkārāsevito [ ]dṛḍha-bhūmiḥ ||1.14|| dṛṣṭānuśravika-viṣaya-vitṛṣṇasya vaśīkāra-saṃjñā vairāgyam||15||
body.translated_text: Of these, practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) is the effort toward steadiness. ||1.13|| But that [practice] becomes firmly grounded when cultivated for a long time, without interruption, and with devotion. ||1.14|| Dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) is the consciousness of mastery in one who is free from craving for objects seen or heard about. ||1.15||
The highest [form of dispassion] is the freedom from craving for the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents of nature), [arising] from the discernment of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self). ||1.16||

<s>Saṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi] (cognitive absorption) is [that which is] accompanied by reasoning (<s>vitarka</s>), reflection (<s>vicāra</s>), bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), and the sense of 'I-am-ness' (<s>asmitā</s>). ||1.17||
The other [<s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>] is preceded by the practice of the cessation [of mental activity], with only <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) remaining. ||1.18||
[For] the <s>videhas</s> (bodiless ones) and the <s>prakṛtilayas</s> (those merged in nature), [it arises from] the condition of [continued] existence. ||1.19||
For others, [it is preceded by] faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), absorption (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). ||1.20||
For those of intense ardor, [<s>samādhi</s>] is near. ||1.21||
A further distinction [arises] according to whether [the ardor is] mild, moderate, or intense. ||1.22||
Or, [<s>samādhi</s> is attained] through devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). ||1.23||
<s>Īśvara</s> is a special <s>Puruṣa</s> untouched by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), actions (<s>karma</s>), fruitions (<s>vipāka</s>), and latent deposits (<s>āśaya</s>). ||1.24||
In Him, the seed of omniscience is unsurpassed. ||1.25||
He is the teacher even of the ancients, because He is not limited by time. ||1.26||
His designator is <s>Praṇava</s> (the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>). ||1.27||
The repetition (<s>japa</s>) of that [<s>Praṇava</s>] and meditation on its meaning [should be practiced]. ||1.28||
From that [practice comes] the attainment of inward consciousness and also the absence of obstacles. ||1.29||

Disease, dullness, doubt, carelessness, laziness, non-abstention, erroneous perception, failure to attain a stage, and instability — these distractions of the mind (<s>citta</s>) are the obstacles. ||1.30||
Suffering, dejection, trembling of the body, and [disturbed] inhalation and exhalation are the accompaniments of distraction. ||1.31||
For their prevention, [there should be] practice on a single principle. ||1.32||

By cultivating friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward the happy, compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) toward the suffering, joy (<s>muditā</s>) toward the virtuous, and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) toward the non-virtuous, the mind (<s>citta</s>) becomes serene. ||1.33||
Or, by the expulsion and retention of breath (<s>prāṇa</s>). ||1.34||

body.text: viṣayavatī vā pravṛttir utpannā manasaḥ sthiti-nibandhanī ||1.35||
body.translated_text: Or, a higher perception arisen with respect to sense objects, producing steadiness of the mind. ||1.35||
Or, [a state that is] sorrowless and luminous. ||1.36||
Or, [by focusing on] a mind free from attachment. ||1.37||
Or, [by taking as] support the knowledge [arising from] dream or sleep. ||1.38||
Or, by meditation on any [object] as desired. ||1.39||
His mastery extends from the most minute atom to the infinitely great. ||1.40||

When the modifications (<s>vṛtti</s>) have dwindled, like a transparent jewel, [the mind] assumes the coloring of whatever [object] — the knower, the knowing, or the known — upon which it rests; this is <s>samāpatti</s> (cognitive absorption). ||1.41||
In that [state], <s>savitarkā samāpatti</s> (absorption with reasoning) is [the condition] mixed with [the distinctions of] word, meaning, and knowledge. ||1.42||
When memory is purified, [the mind,] as if empty of its own form, shining forth as the object alone — that is <s>nirvitarkā</s> (absorption without reasoning). ||1.43||

body.text: etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣma-viṣayā vyākhyātā ||1.44||
body.translated_text: By this same [explanation], <s>savicārā</s> (with reflection) and <s>nirvicārā</s> (without reflection) [absorptions], having subtle objects, are also explained. ||1.44||
And the domain of subtle objects extends up to the unmanifest (<s>aliṅga</s>). ||1.45||
These alone constitute <s>sabīja samādhi</s> (absorption with seed). ||1.46|| Upon the attainment of clarity in <s>nirvicāra</s> [absorption], there is the luminosity of the inner Self. ||1.47||
There, the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is truth-bearing (<s>ṛtaṃbharā</s>). ||1.48||
Its scope is different from [the knowledge gained through] scripture and inference, because it has a particular [direct] object. ||1.49||
The <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) born of that [truth-bearing wisdom] obstructs other <s>saṃskāras</s>. ||1.50||
Upon the cessation of even that [<s>saṃskāra</s>], from the cessation of all [modifications], [there arises] <s>nirbīja samādhi</s> (seedless absorption). ||1.51||

children.translated_text: Austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (<s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s>) constitute <s>Kriyā-yoga</s> (the yoga of action). ||2.1||

body.translated_text: [Thus ends the First Quarter, the <s>Samādhi Pāda</s> (Chapter on Absorption), in the <s>Yoga Sūtra</s> composed by <s>Patañjali</s>.]
[<s>Kriyā-yoga</s>] is for the purpose of cultivating <s>samādhi</s> and for attenuating the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). ||2.2||
The afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) are: ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), egoism (<s>asmitā</s>), attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and clinging to life (<s>abhiniveśa</s>). ||2.3||
Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the field [for the growth] of the others, whether dormant, attenuated, interrupted, or fully active. ||2.4||
Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the perception of the eternal in the non-eternal, of the pure in the impure, of pleasure in suffering, and of the Self in the non-Self. ||2.5||
Egoism (<s>asmitā</s>) is the apparent identification of the power of seeing with the power of the instrument of seeing. ||2.6||
Attachment (<s>rāga</s>) is that which follows upon pleasure. ||2.7|| Aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) is that which follows upon suffering. ||2.8||
Clinging to life (<s>abhiniveśa</s>), flowing along by its own momentum, is rooted thus even in the wise. ||2.9||
These [afflictions], when subtle, are to be overcome by [tracing them back to their] origin (<s>pratiprasava</s>). ||2.10||
Their modifications are to be overcome by meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). ||2.11||
The reservoir of <s>karma</s>, rooted in the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), is experienced in seen [present] and unseen [future] births. ||2.12||
As long as the root [of afflictions] exists, its fruition [manifests as] birth, lifespan, and experience. ||2.13||
These [fruitions] have joy or sorrow as their fruits, according to whether the cause is virtue or vice. ||2.14||

body.text: pariṇāma-tāpa-saṃskāra-duḥkhair guṇa-vṛtti-virodhāc ca duḥkhameva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ ||2.15||
body.translated_text: To the discerning one, everything is suffering indeed, due to the suffering inherent in change, in anguish, and in <s>saṃskāras</s>, and due to the conflict of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents of nature). ||2.15||
The suffering that has not yet come is to be avoided. ||2.16||
The conjunction of the Seer and the Seen is the cause [of suffering] to be avoided. ||2.17||

The Seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) has the nature of illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>), activity (<s>kriyā</s>), and stability (<s>sthiti</s>); it consists of the elements and the sense organs; and its purpose is experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). ||2.18||
The stages of the <s>guṇas</s> are: the particularized (<s>viśeṣa</s>), the unparticularized (<s>aviśeṣa</s>), the undifferentiated (<s>liṅgamātra</s>), and the unmanifest (<s>aliṅga</s>). ||2.19||
The Seer (<s>draṣṭā</s>) is pure consciousness alone, yet [appears to] see through the coloring of the intellect. ||2.20||
The very essence of the Seen exists solely for the sake of that [Seer]. ||2.21||

body.text: kṛtārthaṃ prati naṣṭam apy anaṣṭaṃ tad, anya-sādhāraṇatvāt ||2.22||
body.translated_text: For one who has attained the purpose [of liberation], it [the Seen] has ceased, yet it has not ceased for others, since it is common [to all]. ||2.22||
The conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is the cause by which the powers of the owner and the owned are apprehended in their true nature. ||2.23||
The cause of that [conjunction] is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). ||2.24||

body.text: tadabhāvāt saṃyogābhāvo hānaṃ. tad dṛśeḥ kaivalyam ||2.25||
body.translated_text: From the absence of that [ignorance comes] the absence of conjunction — that is the cessation (<s>hāna</s>). That is the absolute freedom (<s>kaivalya</s>) of the Seer. ||2.25||
Unwavering discriminative discernment (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) is the means of cessation. ||2.26||
For that [Seer], the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) in its final stage is sevenfold. ||2.27||
Through the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>, upon the destruction of impurity, [arises] the light of knowledge, [leading] up to discriminative discernment (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>). ||2.28||

Restraints (<s>yama</s>), observances (<s>niyama</s>), posture (<s>āsana</s>), breath control (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>), withdrawal of the senses (<s>pratyāhāra</s>), concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and absorption (<s>samādhi</s>) are the eight limbs. ||2.29|| Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truthfulness (<s>satya</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>) are the restraints (<s>yama</s>). ||2.30||
When not limited by birth, place, time, or circumstance, [the restraints constitute] the great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>), [applicable] universally. ||2.31||

Cleanliness (<s>śauca</s>), contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (<s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s>) are the observances (<s>niyama</s>). ||2.32||
When disturbed by negative thoughts, [one should cultivate] their opposites (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvana</s>). ||2.33||

Negative thoughts such as violence, whether performed, caused to be performed, or approved; whether preceded by greed, anger, or delusion; whether mild, moderate, or intense — [the reflection that] their fruits are endless suffering and ignorance constitutes the cultivation of the opposite (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvana</s>). ||2.34||
When non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is firmly established, hostility ceases in [the yogi's] presence. ||2.35||
When truthfulness (<s>satya</s>) is firmly established, actions and their fruits become dependent [on his words]. ||2.36||
When non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>) is firmly established, all jewels present themselves [to the yogi]. ||2.37||
When celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) is firmly established, vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is gained. ||2.38||
When steadfast in non-possessiveness (<s>aparigraha</s>), [there arises] the understanding of the 'how' and 'wherefore' of births. ||2.39||
From cleanliness (<s>śauca</s>) [arises] disgust toward one's own body and non-contact with others. ||2.40||
And [from cleanliness arise] purity of <s>sattva</s>, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses, and fitness for the vision of the Self. ||2.41||
From contentment (<s>saṃtoṣa</s>), unsurpassed happiness is gained. ||2.42||
From austerity (<s>tapas</s>), due to the destruction of impurities, perfection of the body and the senses [is attained]. ||2.43||
From self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) [comes] communion with the desired deity (<s>iṣṭa-devatā</s>). ||2.44||
From devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (<s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s>) [comes] the perfection of <s>samādhi</s>. ||2.45||
Posture (<s>āsana</s>) should be steady and comfortable. ||2.46||
[<s>Āsana</s> is perfected] by the relaxation of effort and by absorption in the Infinite. ||2.47||
From that, [one is] not assailed by the pairs of opposites. ||2.48||
When that [posture] is [established], <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) is the interruption of the flow of inhalation and exhalation. ||2.49||
[<s>Prāṇāyāma</s>] manifests as external, internal, and suspended [breathing]; it is regulated by place, time, and number, and becomes prolonged and subtle. ||2.50||
The fourth [type of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>] transcends the external and internal spheres. ||2.51||
From that, the covering of the light is dissolved. ||2.52||
And the fitness of the mind for concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) [is attained]. ||2.53||
Withdrawal of the senses (<s>pratyāhāra</s>) is, as it were, the imitation by the senses of the mind's own nature, when they are disjoined from their respective objects. ||2.54||
From that [arises] the supreme mastery over the senses. ||2.55||
[Thus ends the Second Quarter, the <s>Sādhana Pāda</s> (Chapter on Practice), in the <s>Yoga Sūtra</s> composed by <s>Patañjali</s>.]

children.translated_text: Concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) is the binding of the mind (<s>citta</s>) to a [single] place. ||3.1||

body.translated_text: Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is the continuous flow of cognition toward that [object]. ||3.2||
That same [meditation], when shining forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own form, is <s>samādhi</s> (absorption). ||3.3||
The three together [<s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>] constitute <s>saṃyama</s> (perfect discipline). ||3.4||
From the mastery of that [<s>saṃyama</s>], the light of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) [dawns]. ||3.5||
Its application is in stages. || 3.6 ||
These three [<s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>] are inner limbs compared to the preceding [five]. || 3.7 ||
Even those are outer limbs with respect to seedless [<s>samādhi</s>]. || 3.8 ||

The suppression and emergence of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of emergence and cessation, connected with the mind at the moment of cessation — this is <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (the transformation of cessation). || 3.9 ||
Its peaceful flow [comes] from <s>saṃskāra</s> (repeated practice). || 3.10 ||
The decline of all-objectness and the rise of one-pointedness in the mind — this is <s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s> (the transformation of concentration). || 3.11 ||
Then again, when the subsided and arisen <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions) are equal — this is <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> (the transformation of one-pointedness) of the mind. || 3.12 ||
By this, the transformations of <s>dharma</s> (property), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (characteristic), and <s>avasthā</s> (state) in the elements and sense organs are explained. || 3.13 ||
The <s>dharmī</s> (substrate) is that which follows the <s>dharmas</s> — whether quiescent, arisen, or indeterminate. || 3.14 ||
The difference in sequence is the cause of the difference in transformation. || 3.15 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the three transformations, knowledge of the past and future. || 3.16 ||
Due to the mutual superimposition of word, meaning, and cognition, there is confusion. By <s>saṃyama</s> on their distinction, knowledge of the cries of all beings. || 3.17 ||
By direct perception of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), knowledge of previous births. || 3.18 ||
From [<s>saṃyama</s> on another's] <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition), knowledge of another's mind. || 3.19 ||
But not with its supporting object, because that is not within the scope [of the <s>saṃyama</s>]. || 3.20 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the form of the body, when the power of apprehension is suspended and the connection between the eye and light is broken — invisibility. || 3.21 ||

body.text: sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma. tat-saṃyamād aparānta-jñānam,ariṣṭebhyo vā ||3.22||
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> is of two kinds: active and dormant. By <s>saṃyama</s> on that — knowledge of death; or from portents. || 3.22 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the others — [corresponding] powers. || 3.23 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on powers — the strength of an elephant and so forth. || 3.24 ||
By directing the light of higher sensory activity — knowledge of the subtle, the concealed, and the distant. || 3.25 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the sun — knowledge of the worlds. || 3.26 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the moon — knowledge of the arrangement of the stars. || 3.27 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the pole star — knowledge of their movement. || 3.28 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the navel center (<s>nābhi-cakra</s>) — knowledge of the arrangement of the body. || 3.29 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the throat pit (<s>kaṇṭha-kūpa</s>) — cessation of hunger and thirst. || 3.30 ||

[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the <s>kūrma-nāḍī</s> (tortoise channel) — steadiness. || 3.31 || [By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the light at the crown of the head — vision of the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings). || 3.32 ||
Or, from <s>prātibha</s> (spontaneous intuition) — everything. || 3.33 ||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the heart — knowledge of the mind. || 3.34 ||

body.text: sattva-puruṣayor atyantāsaṃkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo [ ] bhogaḥparārthatvāt svārtha-saṃyamāt [ ] puruṣa-jñānam ||3.35|| tataḥ prātibha-śrāvaṇa-vedanādarśāsvāda-vārtā jāyante ||3.36||
body.translated_text: Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is a cognition that does not distinguish between <s>sattva</s> (intelligence) and <s>puruṣa</s> (pure consciousness), which are utterly distinct. Because [<s>sattva</s>] exists for the sake of another, by <s>saṃyama</s> on what exists for its own sake — knowledge of <s>puruṣa</s>. || 3.35 || From that arise <s>prātibha</s> (intuitive), <s>śrāvaṇa</s> (auditory), <s>vedanā</s> (tactile), <s>ādarśa</s> (visual), <s>āsvāda</s> (gustatory), and <s>vārtā</s> (olfactory) [supernatural perceptions]. || 3.36 ||
These are obstacles to <s>samādhi</s>. In the state of emergence, they are powers. || 3.37 ||
By the loosening of the cause of bondage and by awareness of the passages [of the mind] — entering another's body. || 3.38 ||
By mastery of <s>udāna</s> (the upward breath) — non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like, and ascension [at death]. || 3.39 ||
By mastery of <s>samāna</s> (the equalizing breath) — blazing radiance. || 3.40 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the relationship between the ear and space — divine hearing. || 3.41 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the relationship between the body and space, and by <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) on the lightness of cotton — passage through space. || 3.42 ||

body.text: bahir akalpitā vṛttir mahā-videhā. tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇa-kṣayaḥ ||3.43||
body.translated_text: An external, non-imagined mental activity is the <s>mahāvidehā</s> (great disembodied state). From that, the destruction of the veil over illumination. || 3.43 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent, and purposive [aspects] — mastery over the elements. || 3.44 ||
From that, the manifestation of <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the other [powers], perfection of the body, and non-obstruction by their properties. || 3.45 ||
Beauty, grace, strength, and adamantine firmness — this is perfection of the body. || 3.46 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on apprehension, essential nature, <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness), inherent connection, and purposiveness — mastery over the sense organs. || 3.47 ||
From that, speed of mind, functioning without instruments, and mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). || 3.48 ||
For one who has merely the discernment of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> — sovereignty over all states of existence and omniscience. || 3.49 ||
From <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) even toward that, upon the destruction of the seed of impurity — <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom). || 3.50 ||
When invited by celestial beings, there should be no attachment or pride, for there is the danger of renewed undesirable connection. || 3.51 ||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the moment and its succession — knowledge born of discrimination. || 3.52 ||
From that, discernment of two things that are alike, when they cannot be distinguished by class, characteristic, or location. || 3.53 ||

body.text: tārakaṃ sarva-viṣayaṃ sarvathā-viṣayam akramaṃ ceti vivekajaṃjñānam ||3.54||
body.translated_text: The knowledge born of discrimination is liberating, encompasses all objects, encompasses all conditions, and is non-sequential — thus [it is described]. || 3.54 ||
When the purity of <s>sattva</s> equals that of <s>puruṣa</s> — <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom). || 3.55 ||
[Thus, in the <s>Yoga Sūtra</s> composed by <s>Patañjali</s>, the third <s>Vibhūti Pāda</s> (chapter on powers).]

children.translated_text: Fourth: the <s>Kaivalya Pāda</s> (chapter on absolute freedom).
<s>Siddhis</s> (attainments) arise from birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, austerity (<s>tapas</s>), or <s>samādhi</s>. || 4.1 ||

body.translated_text: Transformation into another form of existence [comes] from the overflow of <s>prakṛti</s> (nature). || 4.2 ||

body.text: nimittam aprayojakaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ. varaṇa-bhedas tu tataḥ kṣetrikavat ||4.3||
body.translated_text: The incidental cause does not set the natural forces in motion. It merely removes the obstacles — like a farmer [removing barriers to the flow of water]. || 4.3 ||
Created minds arise from <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) alone. || 4.4 ||
Among the many [created minds], one mind is the director of the diverse activities. || 4.5 ||
Of these, that which is born of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is free from latent deposits. || 4.6 ||
The <s>karma</s> of a <s>yogin</s> is neither white nor black. Of others, it is threefold. || 4.7 ||
From that, the manifestation of only those <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) that correspond to the fruition of that [<s>karma</s>]. || 4.8 ||
Because <s>smṛti</s> (memory) and <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) are of one form, there is an unbroken continuity even among those separated by birth, place, and time. || 4.9 ||
And they are beginningless, because the will to live is eternal. || 4.10 ||
Since they are held together by cause, effect, substratum, and object — in the absence of these, there is the absence of those [<s>vāsanās</s>]. || 4.11 ||
The past and future exist in their own form, due to the difference in the paths of the <s>dharmas</s> (properties). || 4.12 ||
They are manifest or subtle, and their nature is the <s>guṇas</s>. || 4.13 ||
The reality of a thing is due to the unity of transformation. || 4.14 ||
Even when the object is the same, the paths of mind and object are distinct, due to the difference in minds. || 4.15 ||

body.text: na caika-citta-tantraṃ vastu tad apramāṇakaṃ tadā kiṃ syāt ||4.16||
body.translated_text: An object is not dependent on a single mind; for if it were not cognized by that mind, what would it then be? || 4.16 ||
An object is known or unknown to the mind depending on whether the mind is colored by it. || 4.17 ||
The modifications of the mind are always known to its lord, <s>puruṣa</s>, because of his changelessness. || 4.18 ||
It [the mind] is not self-illuminating, because it is an object of perception. || 4.19 ||
And there cannot be cognition of both [the mind as perceiver and as perceived] at the same time. || 4.20 ||
If one mind were perceived by another, there would be an infinite regress of cognitions of cognitions, and confusion of memory. || 4.21 ||
When consciousness (<s>citi</s>), which does not pass from one state to another, assumes the form of that [mind] — there is awareness of one's own cognition. || 4.22 ||
The mind, colored by the seer and the seen, [comprehends] all objects. || 4.23 ||
That [mind], though variegated by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s>, acts for the sake of another [<s>puruṣa</s>], because it operates in conjunction. || 4.24 ||
For one who sees the distinction [between <s>sattva</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>], there is complete cessation of the cultivation of the notion of self. || 4.25 ||
Then the mind, inclined toward discrimination, gravitates toward <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom). || 4.26 ||
In the intervals of that [discriminative knowledge], other <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions) arise from <s>saṃskāras</s>. || 4.27 ||
Their removal is said to be like that of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). || 4.28 ||
For one who has no self-interest even in the highest meditation, from the constant discernment of discrimination — the <s>dharma-megha samādhi</s> (cloud of dharma concentration). || 4.29 ||
From that, the cessation of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s>. || 4.30 ||
Then, because of the infinity of knowledge freed from all coverings and impurities, what remains to be known is little. || 4.31 ||
From that, the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇas</s>, having fulfilled their purpose, comes to completion. || 4.32 ||
Sequence (<s>krama</s>) is the counterpart of the moment, apprehensible at the end of a transformation. || 4.33 ||

body.text: puruṣārtha-śūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ,sva-rūpa-pratiṣṭhā vā citi-śaktir[] iti [ ] ||4.34||
body.translated_text: The re-absorption of the <s>guṇas</s>, now devoid of purpose for <s>puruṣa</s> — this is <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom), the establishment in one's own nature, or the power of pure consciousness (<s>citi-śakti</s>). || 4.34 ||
[Thus, in the <s>Yoga Sūtra</s> composed by <s>Patañjali</s>, the fourth <s>Kaivalya Pāda</s> (chapter on absolute freedom).]
[Thus, the <s>Pātañjala Yoga Sūtras</s>.]

35. #śakter KSS.
